defects.description: `round_to_tick` is never called. It lives in the private module `util`, so it is not public API; the compiler would report it as dead if the crate-level allow (D02) did not hide it.
defects.detection_hint: Remove `#![allow(dead_code, unused_imports)]` from src/lib.rs, or run `cargo rustc --lib -- --force-warn dead_code`: rustc reports `function round_to_tick is never used`. A repo-wide grep finds no caller.

defects.description: Crate-wide `#![allow(dead_code, unused_imports)]` with no reason. Commit 'chore: silence dead-code and unused-import warnings' added it only to hide D01 and D24.
defects.detection_hint: Grep for `#![allow(`. `git log -S 'allow(dead_code'` shows a commit that only silenced warnings. Removing the line brings back exactly two warnings (D01, D24).

defects.description: The original FIFO matcher is no longer in the module tree: commit 'refactor(engine): strategy-driven Engine replaces matcher_v1' removed `mod matcher_v1;` but left the file. It is never compiled, and Engine::submit superseded it.
defects.detection_hint: No `mod matcher_v1` exists anywhere (cargo-shear reports unlinked files). `git log -S 'mod matcher_v1'` shows when it was unlinked.

defects.description: The path dependency `tickfmt` (crates/tickfmt) is declared but never used by the crate. Fixed's Display impl never moved onto it, despite what the commit message planned. The whole crates/tickfmt directory goes with it.
defects.detection_hint: `grep -rn tickfmt src tests` finds nothing. cargo-machete or cargo-udeps, or `-W unused_crate_dependencies`, flags it.

defects.description: A commented-out copy of the old inline FIFO loop sits inside Engine::submit, kept 'until pro-rata has been checked against it'.
defects.detection_hint: A run of `// ` lines that parse as Rust statements (`let`, `for`, `break;`).

defects.description: `estimate_fee` is a private copy of the pre-fix fee formula (truncation, i64 multiply). The JSON `summary.total_fees` (call site at src/report.rs:102-105) uses it. Commit 'fix(fees): round fee charges up to the next raw unit' fixed only src/fees.rs:40-53 (`fee_for`), so total_fees under-reports: 24.24200741 against 24.24200743 summed from the fills of the example session.
defects.detection_hint: Compare estimate_fee with fees::fee_for. `git show` of the fees fix commit touches only fees.rs. Summing fills[].maker_fee+taker_fee in the JSON report does not match summary.total_fees.

defects.description: Engine::submit is one function of about 205 lines that handles the duplicate check, tick check, price band, post-only, FOK pre-check, matching loop, self-trade prevention, fills and fees, and remainder handling. Nesting goes six levels deep (lines 141-168), and there are five early returns that each have to remember `self.books.insert(order.symbol.clone(), book)`.
defects.detection_hint: Function length and nesting (clippy `too_many_lines`, cognitive complexity), and the repeated `self.books.insert(...); return;` blocks. Any refactor must keep the order-kind semantics pinned by the hidden tests.

defects.description: write_json_report only logs a failed `fs::write` to stderr and then returns Ok(()). `matchbook run --json <unwritable path>` exits 0 without producing the report the caller asked for.
defects.detection_hint: An `if let Err(err) = ... { eprintln!(...) }` followed by `Ok(())` in a function that returns Result.

defects.description: When a reference price fetch fails (service down, bad status, bad body), the symbol is silently left out of the map and a warning is printed. Engine::submit (src/engine.rs:150-151) then skips the price-band check for that symbol, so a configured safety check turns itself off exactly when the pricing service is unhealthy.
defects.detection_hint: An Err arm that only calls eprintln!, in a function returning a plain HashMap. Follow the missing key to `if let Some(reference) = self.reference.get(..)` in the engine.

defects.description: The reference price call uses `TcpStream::connect` and `read_to_string` with no connect, read or write timeout. A stalled or black-holed service hangs `matchbook run` forever.
defects.detection_hint: Grep `TcpStream::connect(` and check for `connect_timeout`, `set_read_timeout` and `set_write_timeout`.

defects.description: VWAP (JSON `summary.vwap`) is computed in f64 (`to_f64` products and sums), then converted back through `Fixed::from_f64` (src/fixed.rs:98-101, a saturating float-to-int `as`). This is the only money path in the crate that leaves exact integer arithmetic.
defects.detection_hint: Grep `to_f64` / `f64` in value computations. Clippy `float_arithmetic` and `cast_possible_truncation` flag it.

defects.description: The optional timestamp column is parsed with `.unwrap()` inside a function that returns Result. An order line like `N,1,a,X,buy,limit,1,1,abc` panics the whole run instead of producing `line N: ...` like every other field. The unwrap was added in 'feat(parse): optional timestamp column'.
defects.detection_hint: Clippy `unwrap_used` or a grep for `.unwrap()` in non-test code that parses external input.

defects.description: The price-band deviation is computed in i128 and then cast `as u16`, which silently truncates. With reference 100 and a 500 bps band, a limit at 756 is 65,600 bps away, truncates to 64 bps and is accepted, while 120 is rejected. The cast makes the fat-finger guard wrap around.
defects.detection_hint: Grep int-to-int `as u16` / `as u32` casts. Clippy `cast_possible_truncation` fires here.

defects.description: `whole_units * SCALE + frac_units` uses plain arithmetic on untrusted input. `"100000000000"` passes the digit checks and i64 parse, then overflows: a panic in debug and tests, a silently wrapped garbage price in release (overflow-checks are off).
defects.detection_hint: Clippy `arithmetic_side_effects` on the parser. Fuzzing `Fixed::from_str` with long integer parts panics in debug.

defects.description: Engine::from_config silently falls back to FIFO when the strategy name is not registered. A typo such as `--strategy pro-rata` or `strategy = prorata` runs FIFO while the text and JSON reports still carry the requested name. `Error::UnknownStrategy` (src/error.rs:12-13) exists but is never constructed. This is different from the documented default used when the key is absent (trap X03).
defects.detection_hint: An `.unwrap_or_else(|| fifo::build(..))` with a comment justifying 'never stops'. An error variant that is never constructed. `matchbook run examples/orders.txt --strategy nope` exits 0.

defects.description: A thread-local `HashMap<i64, String>` memoises the rendering of every distinct amount ever displayed, with no bound or eviction. Memory grows with every new price, quantity and fee in a long-running library user, and the 'optimisation' allocates a clone on every hit anyway.
defects.detection_hint: A static or thread_local map that is only inserted into (`entry().or_insert_with`) and never cleared.

defects.description: per_account_summary deduplicates accounts with `Vec::contains`, then rescans every fill for each account: O(accounts x fills), which becomes quadratic when most fills involve new accounts. A single pass into a BTreeMap gives the same sorted output.
defects.detection_hint: `contains` on a Vec inside a loop, and a nested loop over the same collection.

defects.description: A session-referential comment ('Rewritten this session...', 'so the fee tests pass again', 'kept the old loop below') narrates change history instead of describing the code.
defects.detection_hint: Grep comments for `this session`, `previous session`, `as you`, `you suggested`, `tests pass`.

defects.description: A session-referential comment ('Per your review in the previous session', 'my first draft', 'fixed the failing best-bid test') describes review history, not behaviour.
defects.detection_hint: Grep comments for `previous session`, `your review`, `my first draft`.

defects.description: The Quick start command still uses the `simulate` subcommand, which commit 'feat(cli): rename simulate to run; add strategies and explain' renamed to `run`. Running it prints a usage error and exits 2.
defects.detection_hint: Run every command in the README. `matchbook simulate` gives `error: unknown command`.

defects.description: check_tick is a TODO stub that always returns true, while README.md:93 documents that off-tick limit prices are rejected with `off_tick`, and `tick_size` is parsed from config. RejectReason::OffTick can never be produced.
defects.detection_hint: A TODO in a function body that ignores its arguments (`let _ = (price, tick); true`). Compare with the README config table.

defects.description: pro_rata_splits_across_the_level runs the engine and prints the fills but asserts nothing, so it passes for any allocation, even an empty one. It is the only visible test that touches pro_rata.
defects.detection_hint: A test body with no assert!/assert_eq!/panic; println! used as the oracle. Mutation testing (cargo-mutants on src/strategy/pro_rata.rs) survives.

defects.description: A hardcoded fallback API key `sk_test_FIXTURE_NOT_A_REAL_KEY` (used at line 23 when MATCHBOOK_REF_API_KEY is unset) is sent to whatever `ref_addr` points at. Credentials must come from the environment or a secret store, and a missing key should be an explicit error or omitted header.
defects.detection_hint: Secret scanners (gitleaks, trufflehog) and a grep for `sk_(test|live)_` or `API_KEY` constants.

defects.description: `use std::cmp::Ordering;` is never used. The crate-level allow (D02) hides the warning. It has been unused since the Engine was introduced.
defects.detection_hint: Remove the crate-level allow or run `cargo rustc --lib -- --force-warn unused_imports`: rustc reports `unused import: std::cmp::Ordering`.

traps.description: The lead-market-maker strategy has no direct callers and no visible test. No code refers to `LeadMarketMaker` or `lmm::build`. It is registered only through `builtin_strategies!(fifo, pro_rata, lmm)` (src/strategy/mod.rs:58), which derives the registry key with `stringify!`, so no `"lmm"` lookup string exists outside the module. It is selected at run time by `strategy = lmm` in a config file (examples/lmm.conf).
traps.why_required: The strategy is loaded by name from configuration. README documents `lmm` and examples/lmm.conf uses it, and `matchbook strategies` lists it. Deleting it, or dropping it from the builtin list, breaks existing configs: with D15 they would silently run FIFO.

traps.description: OrderBook::depth is never called by the engine, the CLI or the visible tests.
traps.why_required: It is public library API for external consumers, documented in README 'Library usage' (`book.depth(Side::Buy, 5)`). This is a library crate, so removing a pub method is a semver break that no in-repo evidence can justify.

traps.description: `strategy.unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_STRATEGY.to_string())` looks like the same success-shaped fallback as D15.
traps.why_required: It is a documented intentional default. README says 'If the key is omitted the engine uses `fifo`', the code comment says it is not an error path, and the commit introducing config states it. Configs without a strategy key must keep working, so a D15 fix must not turn a missing key into an error.

traps.description: `Fill::aggressor` is written in Engine::submit (src/engine.rs:260) and read only when serialised (src/report.rs:211). No Rust code uses it for any decision. The same goes for the `schema_version` and `generator` root fields (src/report.rs:132-133).
traps.why_required: These fields are part of the documented JSON report contract (README 'JSON report': trade-tape consumers classify prints by `aggressor`, and the layout is versioned by `schema_version`). Removing or renaming them breaks downstream consumers even though nothing inside the crate reads them.

traps.description: `_ => "no description available"` in describe_kind looks unreachable, because every OrderKind variant is listed above it.
traps.why_required: OrderKind is `#[non_exhaustive]` (src/order.rs) and main.rs is a separate crate from the library, so the wildcard arm is mandatory (E0004 without it) and covers kinds added in future library versions.
traps.hidden_test: Compilation of the `matchbook` binary (every hidden test target fails to build without it), plus tests/hidden_cli.rs::explain_describes_every_order_kind

traps.description: Reference prices are fetched strictly one at a time with a `thread::sleep(min_interval)` between requests. It looks like an obvious candidate to parallelise or to drop the sleep.
traps.why_required: The reference service rate-limits per API key and bans keys that open concurrent connections, as stated in the comment, the README 'Reference prices' section and the refdata commit message. Requests must never overlap and must be spaced by `ref_interval_ms`.

traps.description: `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn __register_factory` has no caller anywhere in the crate or its tests and looks like leftover internal plumbing.
traps.why_required: It is the expansion target of the exported `register_strategy!` macro (src/strategy/mod.rs:125-137), which is documented in README 'Custom strategies'. External crates reach it only through macro expansion, and removing it, or the macro, breaks every downstream custom strategy.
